title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.73-75). X is a variety over a field K, with Γ = Gal(K̄/K). For a 1-connected (simply connected) region T ⊂ X(C), say a real interval or a disc containing K-rational points, Grothendieck uses T itself as a 'thick base point'. This gives a profinite fundamental group Π_T = π_1(X;T) carrying a Γ-action. For x, y ∈ T_K (the K-points in T), take the étale path class γ_{y,x} defined by any topological path inside T. Since T is simply connected, this class is canonical. Its Galois defect g^T_{y,x}(u) ∈ Π_T (u ∈ Γ) satisfies a multiplicativity (cocycle) formula (19). It is functorial: g^{T'}_{f(y),f(x)} = π_1(f)(g^T_{y,x}).

A cover X = ∪_α T_α is indexed by a poset I, ordered by inclusion. For T_α ⊂ T_β there are transition maps φ_{βα} with g^β = φ_{βα}(g^α). The poset satisfies the condition T_α ∩ T_β = ∪_{γ ≤ α,β} T_γ.

On this page Grothendieck adds two hypotheses:
- Connectivity: if T_α and T_β lie in the same connected component of X, there is a chain of indices i_0 = i, …, i_n = j in which consecutive members are comparable (T_k ⊂ T_{k'} or the reverse). The margin rephrases this as π_0(I) → π_0(X) being bijective.
- Covering: the interiors of the T_α cover X (variant: the T_α are closed and A is finite).

Claim: the family of local Galois cocycles g^α_{y,x}(u) ∈ Π_α (α ∈ A, x, y ∈ T_{αK}) determines all the global invariants g_{y,x}(u), i.e. the whole Galois action on the fundamental groupoid of X based at K-points.

Proof. Let p_α : T_α ↪ X be the inclusion. The arrows l^α_{y,x} = p_α(l_{y,x}) generate the fundamental groupoid Π_1(X) restricted to the points X_K. Form the abstract groupoid G with generators l^α_{y,x} and relations l^β_{y,x} = φ_{βα}(l^α_{y,x}); it is the colimit of the trivial groupoids on the T_{αK} over the poset I. The canonical functor G → Π_1(X_K) is bijective on π_0 (by the chain condition) and surjective on π_1 (by generation), so Galois equivariance on G determines it on Π_1. When the interiors cover X there is a simpler argument (completed on p.76): every path is a composite of 'direct' paths between nearby points lying in a common T_α, so the g^α give g_{y,x} for neighbouring points and hence for all points. The closed case is handled by a standard descent argument.

Purpose: a Seifert–van Kampen-type localisation of the Γ-action on π_1. Global Galois action is reduced to finitely many local cocycles attached to simply connected pieces, of which Ihara's f_σ for the real segment [0,1] in P^1 − {0,1,∞} is the prototype. This is a step toward the 'lego' / two-level description of the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower.
errors: The π_0-bijectivity and the generation argument need enough K-rational base points: each T_α, and each overlap used in a chain or in the 'nearby points' argument, must contain points of X_K (or of the chosen base-point set I_α of p.76). This is not stated here; the next page partly addresses it by working with π_1(X,I) for arbitrary base-point sets.

The text asserts only surjectivity on π_1 for G → Π_1(X_K), which suffices for the determination claim. With the intersection condition and an open cover, a Brown-style groupoid van Kampen gives an isomorphism after profinite completion. The page does not need this, but the weaker statement is not optimal.

The draft is heavily crossed out and the hypotheses are revised mid-page: first a chain condition, then interiors covering, then a finite closed cover. The final precise hypotheses are only settled on p.76.

ideas.what: Simply connected regions T ⊂ X(C) used as Galois-stable thick base points, with Galois cocycles g^T_{y,x}(u) measuring the defect of the Γ-action on canonical paths between rational points of T
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale path torsors; tangential/real-segment base points; Ihara's f_σ / Drinfeld–Ihara cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986-91), Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'), Anderson–Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), qualitatively (base points, Galois action on the Teichmüller tower); no cocycle formalism there

ideas.what: The groupoid generated by local path classes over a poset-indexed cover with T_α∩T_β = ∪T_γ maps bijectively on π_0 and surjectively onto the fundamental groupoid
ideas.modern_name: Seifert–van Kampen theorem for groupoids with many base points (colimit over a cover)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX has van Kampen/descent for π_1; groupoid version unsure

ideas.what: Consequence: finitely many local Galois cocycles on simply connected pieces determine the whole Γ-action on π_1(X) and on the fundamental groupoid
ideas.modern_name: Local-to-global determination of the Galois action (in the spirit of the lego/two-level principle for GT)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme gives the lego philosophy but not this cocycle/cover statement

ideas.what: Closed finite covers handled by a descent argument instead of the path-subdivision argument
ideas.modern_name: Van Kampen for closed covers via descent
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exposé IX (descent for étale covers)

missed.claim: The page sketches a general 'Galois van Kampen' principle. For an arbitrary variety X, a poset of simply connected regions with finitely many K-points determines the full Γ-action on the fundamental groupoid through local cocycles g^α_{y,x}(u) and transition maps. The later literature treats concrete cases (P^1 minus points, M_{g,n} via tangential base points) rather than this general formalism.
missed.quote: il suffit de noter que la connaissance des g^α_{y,x}(u) nous donne les g_{y,x}(u) (sans exposant α!) pour x, y points "voisins" sur X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a systematic way to present the Galois action on π_1 of a general curve or moduli space by finitely many local data (e.g. real cell decompositions). This is relevant to explicit Galois/GT actions and to motivic or ℓ-adic periods attached to real cell decompositions. It is close to, but more general than, Ihara/Nakamura computations.

deep.surprise_reason: The van Kampen part is standard (Brown's groupoid version). Using simply connected regions as base points to localise the Galois action is in the spirit of the Esquisse and of later Ihara/Deligne/Nakamura work. The general cover formalism is a mildly notable unpublished detail, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Opening likely reads: '(notamment la surjectivité ... est acquise) que si T_α, T_β sont dans une même comp. connexe de X, il existe une "chaîne d'indices" i_0 = i, i_1, …, i_n = j'.
'on ait T_k ∩ T_{k'} → T_k, … ∩ T_{k'}' should be 'on ait T_k ⊂ T_{k'} ou T_{k'} ⊂ T_k'.
Margin: 'Π(A) → π_0(X)' is probably 'π_0(A) ⥲ π_0(X)' (bijection), with '(A fini)' and 'les T_α soient fermés'.
'de relations tous les invariants g_t^{(u)}' is likely '[détermine] tous les invariants g_{y,x}(u)'.
'Π_1(X_π)' is likely 'Π_1(X_K)', the fundamental groupoid restricted to K-rational points.
'f_e(u)' is uncertain; possibly 'g_{y,x}(u)' or an f_σ-type notation.
'il fait une générat.' is likely 'il fait une application'.
